pool.title: Pooling is the main entrance
pool.body: Four things happen at the moment we buy. You just pull.

batch.title: Batched pulls
batch.body: Refill intents in the same window merge into one request, and volume reaches the vendor's cheaper tier.

vendors.title: Six vendors, one account
vendors.body: One runs dry or goes down, we switch to another. You never watch for it.

compare.title: Effective cost, not sticker price
compare.body: We normalise price over average lifespan, so you compare how long each credit lasts.

refill.title: Dead keys refill
refill.body: A key dies, a fresh one enters the bus. Warranty cases refund credit to your wallet.

auto.title: Keys land, we push
auto.body: Point us at a webhook. Pull completions, dead keys and warranty refunds all arrive there.
auto.apikey: Scripts hit /api/me/* with an API key to pull, route keys, and read the ledger.

dest.title: Three places a key can go

bus.title: Into the bus
bus.body: The key joins a pool. Everyone on the bus uses it and splits the price.

pool.title: To your own pool
pool.body: Syncs to your own pool automatically, with usage data flowing back.

handoff.title: Straight to you
handoff.body: We hand over the plaintext and delete our copy right after.

q1.a: No. Vendor key cost passes through untouched. We charge one technical service fee on top.

q2.q: What happens when a key dies?
q2.a: The bus pulls a replacement automatically. If it falls under warranty, the credit goes back to your wallet.

q3.a: No. You can pull on your own and route the key yourself. Pooling is simply cheaper.

q4.q: Can keys sync to my own pool?
q4.a: Yes. Add your pool URL and token in settings, and every key we pull gets pushed there.

q5.q: Is there an API for scripts and bots?
q5.a: Yes. Create an API key for /api/me/*, then add a webhook to receive events.

cta.title: Find a bus, start saving
cta.body: Sign-up is free. A promo code makes pooling cheaper still.
